messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] extract function and texreg
messages.body_plain:
Hi Christopher,

Thanks for the note, I've opened an issue on GitHub: https://github.com/michaelhallquist/MplusAutomation/issues/44
If you subscribe to that, you should get notified whenever I get around to implementing a work around and closing the issue.

For the moment, your best bet is to pass custom coefficient names.

In a way, I think it would be easiest to deal with in texreg() by adding an argument that optionally escapes any special characters.  This could be turned off by default in case users escaped the characters themselves, but turned on by an optional argument in the case where users have not escaped the characters.
The challenge with doing this on the MplusAutomation side is that if I always escape things like _ and $, then when you use screenreg() you will have pretty ugly output.

The 'solution' from our end is likely to be an optional argument to extract() or coef() methods, something like 'escapeLaTeX = TRUE/FALSE'.  The only other option that comes to mind is to simply strip those characters from the coefficient names and break with Mplus tradition.

It will probably take some time before I get around to implementing any of these as I'm quite busy at the moment.  It would be nice to have a rough solution to make it easy.  For publication quality, I suspect you will always end up passing custom coefficient names as Mplus' variable name restrictions issues around thresholds, multiple groups, and multilevel models makes it almost impossible to automatically have nicely named coefficients appropriate for a journal.

Best wishes,

Josh

messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] Re: Suggestion: Drop this forum and move to StackOverflow
messages.subject_clean: [MplusAutomation] Re: Suggestion: Drop this forum and move to StackOverflow
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I do not have a strong opinion one way or another, but would also be interested in more input or to hear different pros/cons.

Something I think we can do next update is note the GitHub link for bug reports on CRAN.  That said, GitHub is only designed to track bugs/feature requests, and is not intended for general support.

I'm not sure whether SO would provide better support, although I do find it more natural for asking / answering questions as they can be edited and related questions closed/linked, which is often helpful for future readers.

In terms of whether highly requested/pressing needs could be identified, the voting system on SO might solve this.  A question like "How do I extract model indirect results using MplusAutomation" could get upvoted by everyone with the same question/wish.  IF appropriately tagged, these would be searchable and sortable, even for answered questions, by those #MplusAutomation questions with the most upvotes.

What I am not confident in is:

(1) Would questions get appropriately tagged?  If not tagged, I'm not sure Michael or I would ever see them.  Someone with >1,500 reputation would need to create an MplusAutomation tag (http://stackoverflow.com/help/privileges/create-tags)

(2) Are there enough MplusAutomation users on SO that users would start answering questions there who do not on the Google forum?

Can any other user(s) on the forum weigh in?

Best wishes,

Josh

On Thu, Feb 23, 2017 at 8:55 AM, michael.hallquist <michael....@gmail.com> wrote:

> Thanks for this suggestion, Chris. As you accurately note, it is not possible for Josh and I to provide detailed support for many questions on the forum given that we are both otherwise busy academics. Our hope in setting up a forum was that other users would potentially help with answering questions.
>
> In my mind, one downside of switching to Stack Overflow is that it would be more difficult to figure out what features or bugs are most pressing for subsequent versions of the package. For example, based on several users' requests to support MODEL INDIRECT, I've recently asked a student in my lab to help develop a parser for this section. I don't believe I would have prioritized this had it not come up in the forums. We have begun to use Github for feature and bug tracking, however, so perhaps that aligns with the idea of eliminating a forum.
>
> Support is a common problem with FOSS and R packages more specifically. I don't see a simple solution to the problem and don't believe that Stack Overflow would be qualitatively better in this case. But I would be interested to hear others' input on how best to approach this challenge.
>
> Best,
> Michael
>
>
> On Sunday, February 19, 2017 at 7:01:29 PM UTC-5, Christopher Bratt wrote:
> > Hi
> >
> > I have had a look at questions and answers, answers are often significantly delayed or simply lacking. MplusAutomation is authored by two persons and it would add substantially to their workload if they were to give the support suggested by the recommendation to use this forum.
> >
> > MplusAutomation is great! It also has limitations and functions do not always work as expected. In order to improve chances for users to get help, I suggest using StackOverflow instead. Some of the questions are simply beginners' questions. Other questions may still be about issues related to R (R functions in general) and could be solved by others than the developers of the MplusAutomation package. The remaining questions could be followed up on by the authors. I think the current use of Google Groups does not serve the interests of posters and I believe it reduces the spreading of MplusAuthomation.
> >
> > No one can expect developers of free software to give support for free. But it is unfortunate if the impression is given that support will be provided when such support is not possible.
> >
> > Kind regards,
> > Christopher Bratt

messages.subject: nobs as a function of two init iteration variables?
messages.subject_clean: nobs as a function of two init iteration variables?
messages.body_plain:
Good afternoon,

I'm attempting to use the handy createModels() function to write a series of input files for a simulation that I'm working on.  The nobs depends on two of the variables I iterate over in the init section: nclusters and clustersize, as the nobs = nclusters*clustersize (balanced clusters).

However, I haven't figured out how to specify this via the syntax.  The few things I've tried end up with errors.

Failed example 1:
[[init]]
...
nclusters = 100 30 20;
clustersize = 20 30;
...
[[/init]]
...
montecarlo:
nobs = [[nclusters]]*[[clustersize]];
...

results in nobs = 100*20; (which makes sense, after I think about it)

Failed example 2:
I defined the nobs via the DEFINE command:

define:
numberoo = [[nclusters]]*[[clustersize]];

montecarlo = numberoo;

This results in an error message because the argument (numberoo) is not an integer.

Any suggestions / thoughts / ideas?  I've looked through the vignette and the solution hasn't yet occurred to me.

Thanks in advance,
Chris Runyon
PhD Student, Quantitative Methods, UT Austin
